summary: Bradford County, PA steel I-S tower built 1934 by CCC workers, staffed into the 1950s, removed 1987; a 2023 hiking guide reports only the tower's concrete footings remain in State Game Lands 36.

facts.design: Steel I-S tower with a stone caretaker's cabin planned beside it
facts.status_note: Removed in 1987 per the register; a hiking guide dated November 2023 says only the tower's concrete footings remain, and an abandoned building stands by the lot
facts.agency: Forestry Department (state); built by Civilian Conservation Corps workers from the LaQuin camp

access.note: In State Game Lands 36; the access road is gated and closed outside hunting season, per a hiking guide

visit.drive_up: Parking at the SGL 36 lot only when the entrance road gates are open, seasonal around hunting season
visit.trail_note: Easy 3-mile out-and-back hike from the SGL 36 lot; the old concrete pillars sit just behind the abandoned building beside the lot

events.note: October 1933: surveyors doing preliminary work on Kellogg Mountain for a fire tower
Register says built in 1934 as a steel I-S tower; December 1934 newspaper says complete and built by CCC workers from the LaQuin camp
Harry W. Wilcox of Monroeton appointed towerman for the new fire tower
Press item says a year-round observer is stationed at the tower
Edward Hoffman of Towanda, keeper of the Kellogg fire tower
100-watt relay station established on the tower; separately, the state installed a UHF radio system for the Susquehanna River basin meant for flood warning and fire protection
James D. Rundell in charge of the Bradford County fire tower
Robert Brennan of Monroeton manning the tower 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day
Register says the steel I-S tower was removed in 1987
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers from 1933 to 1939 give 80 feet (height_m 24.4). The 1969 NGS station description gives 85 feet. We keep 80 feet, which the press uses consistently, and note the 85-foot figure.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced from 1933-1952 newspaper items reproduced on Forest Lookouts; the removal date (1987) comes only from the register. Today's condition comes from one user-written hiking guide (MyHikes), dated November 04, 2023 and updated January 02, 2024; it does not say when its author visited, and it is the only source for the footings and the building by the lot. The guide calls the building a fire tower house; the 1933 item's stone caretaker's cabin may be the same building, which the story says is unconfirmed. The MyHikes guide mentions the hunting warning but the text we read was cut off before the rest of it. The brief's height 24.4 m is 80 feet and matches the press, not the 85-foot NGS figure. Access 'restricted' reflects the seasonal gate; no source says whether pedestrians can walk the road when gated. The brief's 'other_names': ['K'] looks like a stray letter from the Forest Lookouts heading 'K ELLOGG MOUNTAIN' and is not a real alternate name; we did not change the brief.
